title: MicroservicePrd:HR

identity.ops_surface: managed through OpenTofu-owned infrastructure, root Makefile bootstrap/install/plan/apply targets, and oya ops surfaces; no manual SSH troubleshooting path

decision_log.decision: Machine-readable PRD JSON is canonical; no new Markdown PRD is introduced.
OpenTofu + Makefile + oya ops are the deployment/ops path; manual SSH troubleshooting is explicitly out of scope.
HR, Payroll, and Accounting are the first children; platform model remains extensible for procurement, compliance, assets, and corporate intelligence.

ADR-0131/ADR-0132 flat microservice layout supersedes earlier tenant-rbac crate naming; HR implementation crates use oya-hr-<bounded-context>-<layer> under oya/hr/crates/; retired microservices/hr paths are compatibility/provenance only.
HR AC-01..AC-03 were implemented in CS-ENT-HR-001; AC-04 leave/payroll impact is implemented in CS-ENT-HR-002; AC-05 sensitive-read purpose/legal-basis policy is implemented in CS-ENT-HR-003.
HR app-layer crate emits metadata-only audit and Workflow dispatch envelopes over the pure employment domain; runtime dispatch, persistence, and cloud adapters remain out of scope.

HR API crate owns serializable DTO contracts and deterministic conversion into employment app/domain inputs; deployed HTTP routing, auth middleware, persistence, and runtime adapters remain out of scope.
HR OpenAPI v1 preview contract aligns to HR API DTO crate shapes for employee onboarding and labor-compliance planning; deployed HTTP runtime and auth enforcement remain out of scope.

HR promotion gates follow ADR-0515: GitHub Actions currently produces the single protected oya-ci-required context for the cloud-ci/oya-ci gate logic, with owned oya-ci as the destination runner/product surface. Jenkins/Prow/Groovy are superseded provenance, not compatibility bridges, and cargo-nextest-only evidence is transitional/local feedback until represented through Buck2-backed or owned-runner gate logic. ArgoCD, Helm, runtime deploy, storage, Workflow execution, and cloud adapters remain out of scope until deployable adapters land.

HR AC-04 leave approval payroll-impact foundation is implemented as pure domain planning plus metadata-only app envelope; Workflow execution, payroll calculation, storage, and cloud adapters remain out of scope.

HR AC-05 sensitive-read policy is implemented as pure purpose/legal-basis evaluation plus metadata-only audit envelope; runtime authorization middleware, data retrieval, storage, and audit-chain emission remain out of scope.

HR sensitive-read policy is exposed through transport-neutral API DTOs and OpenAPI 3.2.0 preview request/response contracts for future cloud adapters; deployed authorization, sensitive data retrieval, storage, and runtime audit emission remain out of scope.

HR leave payroll-impact planning is exposed through transport-neutral API DTOs and OpenAPI 3.2.0 preview request/response contracts for future payroll/cloud adapters; leave balance calculation, payroll calculation, storage, Workflow execution, and runtime audit emission remain out of scope.

HR runtime adapter crate binds HR API DTOs to the repo-native Hyper router/middleware foundation and returns OpenAPI-aligned JSON responses; it is router-ready but does not deploy a listener, persist state, execute Workflow, call Payroll, retrieve sensitive HR data, or emit runtime audit-chain events.

HR in-memory storage adapter defines the metadata persistence seam and idempotency behavior for later durable Postgres/RLS or cloud adapters; it is volatile test/local reference storage and does not attach runtime writes, durable storage, Workflow execution, Payroll calls, sensitive-data retrieval, or audit-chain emission.

HR statutory labor rulepacks are represented first as source-versioned manifest provenance in the HR domain; this prepares later cloud/workflow/durable adapters without claiming Workflow execution, payroll calculation, filing transport, cloud deployment, production statutory correctness, or runtime audit-chain emission.

HR PRD test_ref paths point at the current oya/hr source tree. The shared manifests-index is a current manifest inventory guarded by oya-gen-microservice-manifests check mode; because no oya/hr/manifest.json exists in this checkout, HR manifest-index insertion is deferred until a serialized source-authority/manifest producer slice authors the HR manifest or an explicit no-standalone row without runtime readiness claims.

HR sensitive-read runtime-boundary requests require tenant/RBAC scope evidence and the HrSensitiveReadPolicyEvaluated audit-event-class contract ref as internal-only metadata. The Rust DTO remains Option-backed for preview compatibility/deserialization, but the bounded runtime boundary fail-closes when either ref is absent or malformed; this remains a metadata-only preview contract with no sensitive HR data retrieval, raw sensitive-data echo, storage persistence, Workflow execution, Payroll call, deployed listener/cloud deployment, or runtime audit-chain emission claim.
